definitions.nws: NWS minor/moderate/major coastal flood thresholds: water levels set by the local NWS forecast office with local emergency managers, based on years of impact monitoring (road closures, flooding of low areas). Minor: low threat of property damage and no direct threat to life. Moderate: elevated threat of property damage and some risk to life. Major: significant threat to life and property.
definitions.nos: NOS minor/moderate/major thresholds: derived by NOAA NOS CO-OPS with one consistent method for all stations (NOAA Technical Report NOS CO-OPS 086, Patterns and Projections of High Tide Flooding), so that stations can be compared. They are not tied to local road or building impacts.
definitions.source: NOAA CO-OPS Metadata API floodlevels and datums resources; descriptions from the NOAA Coastal Inundation Dashboard FAQ at https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/inundationdb/

result.reference_datum_note: The metadata API does not state the datum of the published values. The Coastal Inundation Dashboard script (https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/inundationdb/assets/js/app.js) subtracts the plotted datum's height above station datum from them, so I treat them as heights above station datum and subtract the MHHW height to get feet above MHHW. Cross-check: the NWS values minus MHHW come out as round numbers (see thresholds above MHHW).
result.retrospective_note: These are the thresholds NOAA publishes now (retrieved 2026-10-25). Applying them to the September 2022 event is a retrospective use, because the values or datums in force in 2022 may have differed.
result.summary: NWS thresholds above MHHW (ft): minor 2.0, moderate 3.5, major 5.0. NOS thresholds above MHHW: minor 1.69, moderate 2.66, major 3.89. Published as heights above station datum, MHHW = 5.68 ft above station datum.
